justification_text:
My point estimates reflect a relatively stable near-term outlook with modest upward drift over longer horizons. For the one-day estimate of 1,268, I was anchoring closely to the most recent observed price level, assuming mean-reverting behavior dominates over very short windows and that no major catalysts were imminent. For the one-week estimate of 1,275, I incorporated a slight positive drift, reflecting the general tendency of risk assets or the underlying instrument to trend modestly higher in the absence of shocks, while also acknowledging that a week is long enough for sentiment shifts to matter. The one-month estimate of 1,290 extends that drift further but also begins to reflect fundamental valuation considerations and any medium-term momentum signals I was weighing at the time of the forecast.

The confidence interval widths reflect how uncertainty compounds with time. At one day, the interval is relatively tight at roughly plus or minus 38 points, because intraday and overnight volatility is fairly predictable in normal market conditions. By one week, the interval widens to plus or minus 75 points, capturing the possibility of scheduled data releases, central bank communications, or geopolitical developments that could shift sentiment meaningfully. At one month, the interval opens considerably to plus or minus 160 points, because over that horizon, entire narratives can shift — economic data can surprise consistently in one direction, policy expectations can reprice, or liquidity conditions can change in ways that are difficult to anticipate from a single starting point.

There are several specific risks that could push outcomes well outside these stated intervals in either direction. On the downside, a sudden deterioration in macro data — such as a sharper-than-expected rise in unemployment, a credit event, or an escalation in geopolitical tensions — could drive prices significantly below the lower bound of the one-month interval. A surprise tightening of financial conditions or a central bank communication that is more hawkish than markets anticipated could also produce outsized moves. On the upside, a strong positive catalyst such as a ceasefire in an ongoing conflict, a dovish policy pivot, or better-than-expected earnings or growth data could push prices well above 1,450 at the one-month horizon. Liquidity events or technical breakouts through key levels could amplify any of these moves beyond what standard volatility models would suggest.
